title: Locally finite abstract cell complex
body_html:
Locally finite abstract cell complex

An [[abstract cell complex|node:abstract_cell_complex.abstract_cell_complex]] $X$ is locally finite when both of the following hold:

  • Finite faces: for every $E \in X$, the down-set $\{F \in X : F \preceq E\}$ is finite.
  • Finite cofaces: for every $E \in X$, the up-set $\{F \in X : E \preceq F\}$ is finite.

Two conditions, one class

At the level of an abstract poset with a dimension function the finite-face and finite-coface conditions are logically independent — neither implies the other without further structure.

They do bundle for a regular CW complex: on a locally finite regular CW complex "each point has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many cells" delivers both simultaneously. Following this geometric convention we bundle them into a single condition, so downstream statements needing either can quote a single hypothesis rather than picking apart the two directions.

Finiteness is genuinely additional data on top of Abstract cell complex: many results (the Alexandrov star topology Alexandrov star topology on the face poset, the order-embedding property of the induction map $\iota$ CW structure and QFD property on G ×^P X') use only the poset and dimension. Only when a summation index or a Finset argument is unavoidable — most prominently the boundary of the cellular chain complex ([[node:representations.chain_complex_C_dot]]) — does local finiteness enter.

Lean formalization

class IsLocallyFinite (X : Type*) [PartialOrder X] : Prop where
  finite_faces   : ∀ E : X, Set.Finite {F : X | F ≤ E}
  finite_cofaces : ∀ E : X, Set.Finite {F : X | E ≤ F}

IsLocallyFinite is a Prop mixin, kept separate from AbstractCellComplex so lemmas that need only the poset and dimension do not depend on finiteness. It takes only [PartialOrder X] (not [AbstractCellComplex X]) so it can be combined with any face-relation structure.
